title: Cognitive Architecture
definition: A hierarchical system of concepts and processes that enables the execution of cognitive functions such as pattern recognition and decision making.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine your brain as a city with many different buildings. Each building represents a different skill, like reading, math, or language. The city layout (cognitive architecture) lets these skills work together to solve complex problems.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Cognitive architecture refers to the organizational structure of a cognitive system, such as an AI agent. It specifies the relationships between cognitive capabilities (e.g., pattern recognition, decision making) and how they are executed in a coherent system.
difficulty_levels.expert: The concept of cognitive architecture originates from cognitive science and AI research. It represents a novel approach to designing AI agents, focusing on the organizational structure of the system rather than individual algorithms. The architecture is IPLD-based and extends the Universal Scientific Concept schema with executable cognitive capabilities for philosophical concept analysis.

extra_fields.insight: The cognitive architecture of an AI agent can be viewed as an extension of the Universal Scientific Concept schema, providing executable cognitive capabilities for philosophical concept analysis.
